name: Thomas White Childs
milestones: Married Edith Van Tyne Adams (m. 11 Sep 1933, Burlingame, California)
Buried at Willamette National Cemetery, Portland, Oregon
career: Graduated from Salem High School and Oregon State College; worked for the federal forest pathology office in Portland (1933).
Graduate work in botany at the University of Pennsylvania on a scholarship, 1933–1936 (styled Dr. Childs by 1936); then assistant in the Forest Pathology office, Portland.
Captain, U.S. Army, World War II.
sources: Ancestry.com, U.S., Veterans' Gravesites, ca. 1775-2019 (Willamette National Cemetery)
Find a Grave, memorial 36261118 (Edith Childs, Willamette National Cemetery)
Ancestry.com, public member tree "Turner / Harvey Family Tree" (tree 67006345)
"Childs Marriage To Take Place Monday", Statesman Journal, Salem, Oregon, 9 Sep 1933, p. 5

Niche marker, Willamette National Cemetery ("Childs, Thomas W, Capt USA, WWII, 1908–1998; Edith Adams, 1912–2000"), photograph in the Turner / Harvey Family Tree on Ancestry.com
notes: Husband of Edith (Adams) Childs, George Francis Adams Sr.'s sister. Born 20 May 1908; died 7 May 1998; a captain in the U.S. Army, buried at Willamette National Cemetery. With Edith and their sons George C. and Gregg E. in Portland in 1940 and 1950.

Son of Mr. and Mrs. C. D. Childs of Salem, Oregon (Statesman Journal, 9 Sep 1933). He left Salem for San Francisco and married Edith Adams at Burlingame on 11 Sep 1933; the couple went straight to Philadelphia, where he did graduate work in botany at the University of Pennsylvania, returning to Portland in June 1936 as assistant in the Forest Pathology office. His niche marker reads "Capt USA, WWII, 1908–1998".
